spec.title: All Receivers
spec.description: Debt, target, balance and idle capital per receiver. Idle = balance - target; receivers with positive idle are not being funded this cycle.

spec.title: Balance/Debt Ratio
spec.description: Total balance as a percentage of total debt. The algorithm targets ~1/balance_fill_factor (125% at 0.8, 167% at 0.6). Sustained readings well above target indicate idle capital.

spec.title: Total Target (GRT)
spec.description: Sum of the target escrow balance the funding algorithm is currently aiming for, across all receivers. Driven by debt and `balance_fill_factor`.

spec.title: Idle Capital (GRT)
spec.description: Escrow balance above what the algorithm is asking for. The manager never withdraws, so this only drains as receivers collect. A large value means drift from past debt, not the current funding margin.

spec.title: Idle Capital by Receiver (Top 10)
spec.description: Balance above target, per receiver. These accounts receive no deposits until their debt grows back into their balance.

spec.title: Dead Escrow (GRT)
spec.description: Escrow held for receivers whose current debt is zero — the unrecoverable share of Idle Capital. These accounts have nothing left to collect and the manager has no withdraw path, so this does not drain on its own. Reads high if the Kafka receipts tally is incomplete.

spec.expr: sum(max by (receiver) (escrow_balance_grt{job=~"$job"}) and max by (receiver) (escrow_debt_grt{job=~"$job"}) == 0) or vector(0)

spec.title: Dead Accounts
spec.description: Receivers holding escrow with zero current debt, usually indexers that closed all their allocations. Compare against Receivers to see how much of the set is inactive.

spec.expr: count(max by (receiver) (escrow_balance_grt{job=~"$job"}) > 0 and max by (receiver) (escrow_debt_grt{job=~"$job"}) == 0) or vector(0)

spec.title: Dead Accounts (debt = 0)
spec.description: Receivers holding escrow with zero current debt, one row each, largest balance first. Peak Debt 7d/30d is the highest debt seen in that window: red (zero) means the account has been inactive for the whole window and its escrow is stranded, green means it was recently active and this is ordinary drift that will drain as the receiver collects. Escrow Balance sums to the Dead Escrow stat in Overview.

spec.title: Thawing (GRT)
spec.description: Escrow currently pending withdrawal back to the payer. Thawing does not reduce the balance and does not stop a receiver collecting; the funds leave only when the 28 day thawing period matures and the withdrawal executes.

spec.title: Accounts Thawing
spec.description: Receivers with escrow pending withdrawal. Compare against Receivers to see how much of the set is being reclaimed from.

spec.title: Thaws Failed
spec.description: Failed `thaw` transactions in the selected range. Thaws start a reclamation; a sustained failure means idle escrow is no longer being reclaimed, which is visible as a flat Thawing line.

spec.title: Withdrawals Failed
spec.description: Failed `withdraw` transactions in the selected range. The escrow contract reverts the whole batch if any thaw has not matured. Maturity is planned against the latest block timestamp, which cannot run ahead of the executing block, so repeated failures point at a receiver collecting mid-cycle rather than at clock drift.

spec.title: Thawing Over Time
spec.description: Total escrow pending withdrawal. Steps up when reclamation starts on a receiver, down as receivers collect against a thawing balance, and to zero as withdrawals mature.

spec.title: Reclamation In Flight
spec.description: Receivers with escrow pending withdrawal, one row each. Thawing is the amount due back to the payer at maturity; it is fixed when the thaw starts and is not resized, so debt growing meanwhile is answered by a deposit instead. Balance minus Thawing is what funding decisions use.

spec.title: Reclamation Transactions
spec.description: Thaws start a reclamation and only fire for receivers with nothing already thawing; withdrawals only fire once a thaw matures. Both are expected to be rare -- a receiver can start at most one thaw per 28 day period.

spec.title: Reclamation Duration
spec.description: Average transaction duration for thaws and withdrawals.
